title: SIGNAL SHACK — Beach Commons V9
dek: Eight group electronics benches, a browser signal rack, charming low-fi, ambitious hi-fi, and no feed required
body:
SIGNAL SHACK remakes the sociable spirit of the old neighborhood electronics counter as a covered public workshop near the coast. It is unaffiliated with RadioShack or any electronics retailer.

Eight group benches run from a passive crystal receiver and repaired cassette loops through certified LoRa mesh-message lanterns, small environmental instruments, receive-only NOAA weather radio, offline local-AI repair assistance, and one collective high-fidelity headphone instrument. Low-fi and hi-fi are not treated as ranks. Each reveals a different layer of how a signal becomes a shared experience.

The human edition includes eight original 1536×1024 visual plates, a thirty-minute bench rotation, eight contributor roles, three paths toward an honest real-world experiment, current official technology sources, and a six-voice browser Signal Rack synthesized live from oscillators and generated noise. There is no sample, recording, auto-play, television, scrolling wall, account, or required cloud connection.

The credible actual version starts with an authorized room—not equipment on open sand. LA County’s Dockweiler Youth Center is one venue inquiry path. Any program would need advance confirmation of the gathering, tools, soldering, batteries, audio, radio equipment, accessibility, insurance, and operating rules. The concept does not announce or promise an event.

Radio work is receive-only or uses certified modules and stock antennas; any amateur transmission belongs with properly licensed operators. Sound stays in headphones or at a permitted indoor level. Batteries stay protected, supervised, and away from saltwater and fire rings. Every small part works over a tray and comes home. Dunes, shoreline passage, emergency access, and western snowy plover habitat remain outside the experiment.

media.alt: A sunset community electronics workshop centered on a branching headphone tree, amber modular audio equipment, patch cables, turntables, repair benches, and silent dancing
